clue.text: High-altitude bases offering exceptional aspect from Alps

indicators.note: exceptional means out of the ordinary, so the letters of these words are set in an unusual new order

explanation.surface: A travel blurb promising a remarkable view from the Alpine heights.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a mountain viewpoint, but the bases are much higher than the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: Space platforms are stations orbiting far above the Earth, serving as bases at extreme altitude.

clue.text: European tax-based changes more than sufficient to encourage antisocial behaviour

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of European's E and tax-based are rearranged

parts.note: ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A grumble that a European tax regime goes too far and breeds bad conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges E plus TAXBASED into SETABADEX, then AMPLE finishes the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a bad example is to model poor conduct that others then copy, so it promotes misbehaviour.

clue.text: Son of David rating peace for Israel — that's not hard

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a naval rating

indicators.note: that's not tells us the letter for the next word is dropped from the peace word

parts.note: shalom is the Hebrew word for peace
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A biblical son weighing up the prospects for peace in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is any ordinary sailor; AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: Absalom was the third son of King David in the Old Testament, who rebelled against his father.

clue.text: Ignoring poll, shouted about celebrity with a glossy exterior

indicators.note: about means placed around the word for celebrity
the poll is the head, so ignoring it means leaving off the first letter

parts.note: yelled means shouted
a name is a famous person, as in a big name

explanation.surface: Someone ignoring an election and shouting at a famous person with a shiny finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poll' is not a vote here but the old word for the head, so only the first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamelled objects are coated with a hard, shiny vitreous layer, giving them a glossy surface.

clue.text: Final flag hoisted above ship's stern, done in desperation at the eleventh hour

definitions.text: done in desperation at the eleventh hour

indicators.note: in a down answer, above puts these letters before the next piece

parts.note: last means final

indicators.note: in a down clue, hoisted means the word for flag is read upwards

parts.note: to flag is to sag or droop

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a ship, so the last letter of ship

explanation.surface: A final flag run up over the stern of a vessel in a last-minute emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoisted' turns SAG upwards to GAS, sitting 'above' P, the 'stern' of ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-gasp effort is a desperate attempt made at the very final moment, as with a dying breath.

clue.text: Corridor covered with it — rising fungus and lichen, say

indicators.note: covered with means the corridor word sits between the letters of it
in a down clue, rising means it is read upwards

parts.note: a hall is a passage or corridor

explanation.surface: A corridor overgrown with fungus and lichen creeping up the walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns IT to TI, and HALL is 'covered with' it. Thalli is the plural of thallus.
explanation.definitionFit: A thallus is the undivided plant body of simple organisms such as fungi, algae and lichens.

clue.text: In seconds, forget about people slain with daggers

indicators.note: in seconds means taking the second letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A grim aside about forgetting people killed with knives, all in moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In seconds' reads like 'very quickly', but asks for the second letter of each of the next five words.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are the dagger-shaped printing marks used to flag footnotes, and also the dagger symbol in reference books.

clue.text: Refuse working with international telecom pioneer

parts.note: marc is the refuse left after pressing grapes
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A rubbish collection firm working with an international telecoms innovator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: marc is grape pulp left over after winemaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi developed long-distance radio transmission, a founding achievement of telecommunications.

clue.text: Deceiving band in double-cross that's been planned throughout

indicators.note: in means the band word goes inside the planned con

parts.note: a sting is an elaborately planned confidence trick
a ring is a band
along can mean through the whole length, throughout

explanation.surface: A gang deceived by a betrayal that was premeditated all along.
explanation.walkthrough: A sting is a carefully set-up con, so the long phrase is a single definition of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringing someone along means misleading them over a period, keeping them hoping or believing falsely.

clue.text: Chap stopping fool in afternoon meal getting some water

indicators.note: in means placed inside the meal word

parts.note: tea is the afternoon meal

indicators.note: stopping means plugging the gap inside the word for fool

parts.note: an ass is a fool
man means chap

explanation.surface: A man interrupting an idiot at teatime who is getting some water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasman Sea is the stretch of the Pacific between Australia and New Zealand, a body of water.

clue.text: Bird regrettably chokes

indicators.note: chokes means the word holds the answer tightly inside it

explanation.surface: A sad note that a bird is choking.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a wading bird.

clue.text: English easy about rubbish

indicators.note: about means the English letter and the word for easy are turned round together

parts.note: glib means effortless, easy

explanation.surface: An English pushover and some rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge, the foul water in a ship's hull, is also slang for nonsense or worthless talk.

clue.text: Bitterness shown by Turkey abandoning Mediterranean port in campaign

parts.note: gall means bitterness, resentment

indicators.note: abandoning means the letters for Turkey leave the port's name

parts.note: Tripoli is a port on the Mediterranean, capital of Libya
TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

explanation.surface: Resentment as Turkey gives up a port during a military campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Turkey is not the bird here but the country, by its international vehicle code.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli was the disastrous 1915-16 Allied campaign on the Turkish peninsula of that name.

clue.text: Ruin, perhaps as a march crushes Left

indicators.note: crushes means the protest pieces squeeze the letter for left between them

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
-ish means roughly or perhaps, as in 'six-ish'

explanation.surface: A protest march squashing the political Left, perhaps ruining it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is not signalling an example here: the suffix -ish means 'more or less'.
explanation.definitionFit: To demolish is to destroy or wreck utterly, as with a building pulled down.

clue.text: Border gradually moving

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a trim or border, as on a lawn or garment
second meaning: moving little by little

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a decorative border and a participle for creeping slowly along.

clue.text: Embellished by dodgy press dude

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A shady journalist adding embellishments to the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed up means made to look more attractive or impressive, adorned or exaggerated.

clue.text: Negative duo that won't bond on record is entering retreat

indicators.note: is entering means the pieces go into the retreat word

parts.note: a lair is a retreat or hideaway
taken as written
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A pessimistic pair, unwilling to commit, who have retreated, as is on record.
explanation.walkthrough: In chemistry a lone pair is two valence electrons not shared in a bond, and electrons are negative.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrons carry negative charge, and a lone pair is two of them not involved in chemical bonding.

clue.text: Idyllic spot in Sudan axed following setback

indicators.note: setback means the hidden letters are read backwards
in means the answer lies inside these words

explanation.surface: A paradise in Sudan cut after a reversal of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Read SUDANAXED backwards as DEXANADUS; the answer is 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanadu, Kublai Khan's summer seat in Coleridge's poem, has come to mean any place of idyllic luxury.

clue.text: Heartless upstart right to cut gas for which there's no charge

indicators.note: to cut means the pieces slice into the gas word

parts.note: neon is a gas

indicators.note: heartless means losing everything but the outer letters

explanation.surface: A tactless upstart with the right to cut off the gas supply for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' upstart gives UT; with R it goes into NEON. The definition is a charge-free particle, not a free supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron is a subatomic particle with no electric charge, found in atomic nuclei.

clue.text: Moderate team primarily needing a goal to equalise?

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter

parts.note: a side needing one goal to draw level is one down

explanation.surface: A football team chasing an equaliser being told to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: T from 'team primarily' plus ONE DOWN, the state of a side one goal behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To tone down is to soften or make less extreme, as a verb sense of moderate.

clue.text: Pseudo switched, heading for interdisciplinary church organisation

indicators.note: switched means the letters change places
heading for means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A sham academic switching to interdisciplinary work for a church body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switched' turns PSEUDO into OPUSDE; the 'heading for' interdisciplinary is I.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus Dei is a Roman Catholic institution, a personal prelature founded in Spain in 1928.

clue.text: Explains about constant contributors to immune response

indicators.note: about means the explaining word wraps around the constant

parts.note: tells can mean explains, as in tells why
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Someone constantly explaining how the body fights infection.
explanation.walkthrough: TELLS goes 'about' C.
explanation.definitionFit: T cells are white blood cells, lymphocytes that play a central part in the body's defence against infection.

clue.text: For example, a toothbrush might initially get rid of persistent pain

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

parts.note: to oust is to get rid of
an ache is a dull, persistent pain

explanation.surface: Using a toothbrush might cure a nagging toothache.
explanation.walkthrough: The toothbrush is not for teeth: a toothbrush moustache is a short square one under the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothbrush is a style of small, clipped, rectangular moustache, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Steak essentially rubbery in quality

indicators.note: in means the middle letter goes inside the quality word

parts.note: tone is a quality, as of sound

indicators.note: essentially means the essence or central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A complaint that a steak is basically chewy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' rubbery is its central letter B, which goes 'in' TONE after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bone is a cut of beef containing a T-shaped bone, a kind of steak.

clue.text: Old bandmaster provided by America

parts.note: so can mean provided that, as in 'so long as'
USA is America

explanation.surface: An old band leader supplied by the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' looks like a verb but is SO in its 'on condition that' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: John Philip Sousa was an American composer of marches who led the US Marine Band.

clue.text: Large old ship that's broad and slow

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A big old vessel that is wide and sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broad and slow' sounds like a description of the ship, but it is the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction meaning to play in a slow, stately, broad manner.

clue.text: Turkey with plain dressing served around northern resort

indicators.note: dressing means the plain word is wrapped like a coat over the other pieces
around confirms the plain word goes round the others

parts.note: a llano is a grassy plain in South America
a turkey is a flop, a dud

explanation.surface: A roast turkey with simple stuffing served at a northern resort.
explanation.walkthrough: A turkey is a flop, not the bird, and a llano is a South American plain. Llandudno is a seaside resort in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Llandudno is a Victorian seaside town on the north Wales coast, a popular holiday resort.

clue.text: Beneath loose pants, grip is inferior

parts.note: under means beneath

indicators.note: loose means the letters are set free to rearrange

explanation.surface: A garment's poor grip under baggy trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Understrapping is a rare word, from understrapper, an underling.
explanation.definitionFit: Understrapping describes someone subordinate or of lower rank, a minor assistant.
